senses.title: The Object in the Mind: the 1610s philosophical sense
senses.titleCN: 心中的对象：17 世纪初的哲学义
senses.definition: in 1610s philosophy, existing as perceived or thought, ideal, representative, or phenomenal, as opposed to subjective or formal
senses.definitionCN: 17 世纪初哲学中，指作为被感知或被思考之物而存在的、观念的、表象的、现象的，与 subjective 或 formal 相对
senses.example: In the old debate, pain was called objective when considered as a thought rather than a bodily state.
senses.exampleCN: 在那场古老争论中，痛苦被当作思想而非身体状态来看时，被称为 objective。
senses.why: The word was built from objectum, 'a thing put before the mind'. In the 1610s that thing was still inside the mind, so objective meant 'existing as an object of thought'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 objectum“被摆到心智面前的东西”构成。17 世纪初，这东西还在心智之内，所以 objective 意为“作为思想对象而存在”。

senses.title: The Real Thing Outside: independent of the mind
senses.titleCN: 心外实物：不依赖心智而存在
senses.definition: real and existing independently of the mind, belonging to the object of knowledge rather than to the observer
senses.definitionCN: 真实存在、不依赖心智的，属于认知对象而非观察者的
senses.example: The mountain has an objective existence whether or not anyone looks at it.
senses.exampleCN: 无论是否有人看它，这座山都客观存在。
senses.why: From the mid-17th century the 'object' was pushed outside: what is objective is what belongs to the thing known, not to the knower. The sense almost reverses the older one.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪中期起，“对象”被推到心智之外：objective 的东西属于被认识的事物，而不属于认识者。这个义项几乎翻转了旧义。

senses.title: Without a Personal Lens: impartial
senses.titleCN: 不戴个人镜片：不偏不倚
senses.definition: not influenced by personal feelings, interests, or bias when judging
senses.definitionCN: 判断时不受个人情感、利益或偏见影响
senses.example: A judge must remain objective even when the case is emotionally charged.
senses.exampleCN: 即使案件牵动情绪，法官也必须保持客观。
senses.why: If truth belongs to the object, the observer should stop adding private colour. The 18th-century sense, strengthened through German translations, names that disciplined detachment.
senses.whyCN: 如果真相属于对象，观察者就该停止添加私人色彩。18 世纪经德语译介强化的义项，命名的正是这种克制的抽离。

senses.title: What the Evidence Shows: fact-based
senses.titleCN: 证据所示：以事实为依据
senses.definition: based on observable facts and evidence that others can check
senses.definitionCN: 建立在他人可以核查的可观察事实与证据之上
senses.example: The report gives an objective account of the accident, with times and measurements.
senses.exampleCN: 报告用时间和测量数据，对事故作了客观陈述。
senses.why: An account is objective when it stays with what was put before the senses: times, measurements, records. Evidence replaces opinion as the measure.
senses.whyCN: 当陈述停留在摆在感官之前的东西——时间、测量、记录——它就是客观的。证据取代意见成为量尺。

senses.title: The Point to Be Taken: a military objective
senses.definition: a place or position that an army aims to capture or hold, from which the general noun use grew
senses.definitionCN: 军队意图夺取或守住的地点或阵地，名词的一般用法由此而来
senses.example: The hill was the objective of the night attack.
senses.exampleCN: 那座山头是夜袭的目标。
senses.why: Military language used objective for the point set before the force, the thing to be taken. The target on the map is literally 'the object put in front'.
senses.whyCN: 军事语言用 objective 指摆在部队前方的点，即要夺取的东西。地图上的目标字面上就是“被摆在前面的对象”。

senses.title: The Aim: a goal to reach
senses.definition: a goal or aim that a person or organization works toward
senses.definitionCN: 个人或组织努力要达到的目标
senses.example: Our main objective is to cut waiting times by half.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的主要目标是把等待时间减少一半。
senses.why: Once the military target became general, any planned end point could be an objective: something placed ahead of you that guides effort.
senses.whyCN: 军事目标一旦泛化，任何计划中的终点都可以叫 objective：一个摆在你前方、引导努力的东西。

senses.title: The Lens Facing the Object
senses.definition: in optics, the lens or lens system nearest the object being viewed, as in a microscope or telescope
senses.definitionCN: 光学中离被观察物体最近的那片透镜或透镜组，如显微镜或望远镜的物镜
senses.example: Clean the objective before examining the slide.
senses.exampleCN: 检查玻片前先清洁物镜。
senses.why: The optical objective is the lens turned toward the object, not toward the eye. The same 'thing before you' image is used in a physical instrument.
senses.whyCN: 光学物镜是朝向物体、而不是朝向眼睛的那片镜片。同一个“摆在面前的东西”的意象被用在一件实体仪器上。

senses.title: The Object Case: grammar
senses.definition: in grammar, the case of a noun or pronoun that is the object of a verb or preposition
senses.definitionCN: 语法中名词或代词作动词或介词宾语时的格
senses.example: In 'she saw him', him is in the objective case.
senses.exampleCN: 在 she saw him 中，him 是宾格。
senses.why: Grammar names the receiver of the action the object. The objective case is simply the form a word takes when it stands as the object before the verb.
senses.whyCN: 语法把动作的承受者称为 object。宾格就是当一个词作为动词的宾语出现时所取的形式。

senses.title: Description Without Interpretation
senses.titleCN: 不带解释的描述：客观呈现
senses.definition: presenting what can be seen or measured without adding interpretation, as in objective reporting or photography
senses.definitionCN: 只呈现可见或可测的内容而不添加解释，如客观报道或客观摄影
senses.example: The photographer took an objective record of the building before demolition.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师在拆除前对建筑作了客观记录。
senses.why: The final extension keeps the observer out of the frame. What is recorded is the object as it stands, with no story laid over it.
senses.whyCN: 最后的延伸把观察者请出画面。被记录的是对象本来的样子，上面没有叠加任何故事。

intro.en: Objective is object plus -ive. Object came from Latin obiectum 'thing put before', and objective first meant 'existing as an object of thought' before its sense moved outside the mind to 'real' and then to 'impartial'.
intro.cn: objective 是 object 加 -ive。object 来自拉丁语 obiectum“被摆到面前的东西”，而 objective 最初指“作为思想对象而存在”，后来移出心智，变成“真实的”，再变成“不偏不倚的”。

items.en: First used as a philosophical term meaning 'as perceived or thought; ideal; representative; phenomenal', opposed to subjective or formal.
items.cn: 最初作哲学术语，意为“被感知或被思考的；观念的；表象的；现象的”，与 subjective 或 formal 相对。

items.en: The sense 'belonging to the real object of knowledge, real' appears, in contrast with subjective; the meaning almost reverses the earlier one.
items.cn: 出现“属于认知的实在对象、真实的”义，与 subjective 相对；含义几乎翻转了早先的义项。

items.en: The modern sense 'unbiased, not shaped by personal feeling' is strengthened through German philosophical translations.
items.cn: 现代义“客观的、不带偏见的”经德语哲学译介而强化。

items.en: Formed on medieval Latin objectivus, used by Duns Scotus, from objectum 'thing put before'.
items.cn: 按中世纪拉丁语 objectivus 构成，邓斯·司各脱曾使用，出自 objectum“被摆到面前的东西”。

items.en: Objectum is the neuter noun use of obiectus, past participle of obicere 'to throw before': ob 'in front of, towards, against' plus iacere 'to throw' (PIE *ye- 'to throw, impel').
items.cn: objectum 是 obiectus 的中性名词化；obiectus 为 obicere“投到前面”的过去分词：ob“在前、朝向、对着”+ iacere“投、掷”（原始印欧语 *ye-“投、推”）。

items.en: The noun 'objective' meaning a target comes from military usage, the point set before a force; the general sense 'goal' followed. Object itself dates from late 14c.
items.cn: 名词 objective 的“目标”义来自军事用语，即摆在部队前方的点；泛化的“目的”义随后出现。object 本身则始于 14 世纪晚期。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the object family and its -ive neighbours; the near-meaning group holds words that overlap with only part of objective.
note.cn: 形近组留在 object 词族及其 -ive 邻词内；近义组是只与 objective 部分义项重叠的词。

entries.definition: a thing that can be seen or touched, or something opposed. Objective is built from it, but the stress and the noun-verb split differ.
entries.definitionCN: 可见可触的物体，或反对的对象。objective 由它构成，但重音和名词／动词分工不同。

entries.definition: a statement of disagreement. It comes from object as a verb 'to oppose', not from objective.
entries.definitionCN: 反对的意见。它来自动词 object“反对”，而不是来自 objective。

entries.definition: a word that describes a noun. It shares the -ive ending and the Latin iacere 'throw' root, but its prefix is ad-, not ob-.
entries.definitionCN: 描述名词的词。它同样以 -ive 结尾，也含拉丁语 iacere“投”的词根，但前缀是 ad-，不是 ob-。

entries.definition: not favouring one side over another. It stresses fairness between parties, while objective stresses independence from one's own feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏袒任何一方。它强调各方之间的公平，objective 强调独立于自己的情感。

entries.definition: free from prejudice or a settled leaning. It is close to objective but names the absence of bias rather than the presence of facts.
entries.definitionCN: 没有偏见或既定倾向。它接近 objective，但说的是“没有偏见”，而不是“依据事实”。

entries.definition: based on facts. It covers only the evidence sense of objective and says nothing about being a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 以事实为依据的。它只覆盖 objective 的证据义，与“目标”义无关。

normalIntro.en: Real links only: objectum is ob- 'before' plus iacere 'to throw', and objective is object plus -ive. The 1610s and modern senses are a recorded reversal, not an invented story.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实联系：objectum 是 ob-“在前”加 iacere“投”，objective 是 object 加 -ive。17 世纪初义与现代义是有记录的翻转，不是编造的故事。

normal.en: Objectum is ob- 'in front of' plus iacere 'to throw': a thing thrown before the mind or the eyes.
normal.cn: objectum 是 ob-“在前”加 iacere“投”：被投到心智或视线之前的东西。

normal.en: Objective is simply object plus -ive: 'relating to the object put before you'.
normal.cn: objective 就是 object 加 -ive：与“摆在你面前的对象”相关的。

normal.en: The 1610s sense meant 'in the mind'; the modern sense moved outside the mind to 'real'. The word reversed direction.
normal.cn: 17 世纪初的义项指“在心中的”；现代义移到心外，指“真实的”。这个词转了个方向。

normal.en: Objection and objective share object but pull opposite ways: one throws something against, the other looks at what is before.
normal.cn: objection 与 objective 都含 object，却朝相反方向拉：一个把东西扔过去反对，一个只看面前的东西。

normal.en: A military objective is the literal point set before a force; the everyday 'goal' grew from that target.
normal.cn: 军事 objective 是字面上摆在部队前方的点；日常的“目标”义从那个靶点长出来。

abstract.en: Picture an object alone under a lamp: the table, the wall and the observer all fall into shadow.
abstract.cn: 想象灯下只有一件东西：桌子、墙和观察者都落进阴影。

abstract.en: The observer steps back until their own shadow leaves the frame; that is the move from subjective to objective.
abstract.cn: 观察者后退，直到自己的影子离开画面；这就是从主观到客观的那一步。

abstract.en: Move the same object onto a map and it becomes a target: objective is now the point to be reached.
abstract.cn: 把同一件东西移到地图上，它就成了靶点：objective 此时是要到达的点。

examples.en: The study offers an objective measure of how noisy the streets are.
examples.cn: 这项研究提供了街道噪声程度的客观量度。

examples.en: Our objective for the year is to reduce waste by a third.
examples.cn: 我们今年的目标是把浪费减少三分之一。

examples.en: He tried to stay objective, but the photographs made him angry.
examples.cn: 他努力保持客观，但那些照片让他愤怒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊不，接个物体」——先别急着评判，把摆在面前的物体接住看清楚 → objective 客观的、目标

root: 拉丁语 objectum“被摆到面前的东西”= ob“在前”+ iacere“投、掷”，加 -ive；objective 字面“与摆在面前的对象相关的”，由“客体”引出“客观”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of objective all turn on one act: throwing something in front. First it is an object of thought, then a real thing outside, then an impartial view, then a target on a map.
sensesIntro.cn: objective 的九个义项都围绕一个动作：把某物投到前方。它先是思想的对象，再是心外的实物，再是不偏不倚的看法，最后成为地图上的靶点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object placed in front of the mind or the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件被摆到心智或视线之前的东西。

branches.en: THE OBJECT IN THE MIND: the 1610s philosophical sense, where the object is still a thought.
branches.cn: 心中的对象：17 世纪初的哲学义，对象仍是一种思想。

branches.en: REALITY AND EVIDENCE: the object outside the mind, and the facts that can be checked.
branches.cn: 现实与证据：心外的对象，以及可以核查的事实。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINED OBSERVER: impartial judgment, and description without interpretation.
branches.cn: 受约束的观察者：不偏不倚的判断，以及不带解释的描述。

branches.en: THE AIM: a military point to be taken, and the general goal that grew from it.
branches.cn: 目标：要夺取的军事据点，以及由此长出的普通目的。

branches.en: TECHNICAL OBJECTS: the lens facing the object, and the grammatical object case.
branches.cn: 技术性对象：朝向物体的镜片，以及语法中的宾格。

intro.en: Objective is the Latin adjective objectivus in English form: object- plus -ive. The root sits in ob- 'before' and iacere 'to throw', the same root that gives subject, adjective and object.
intro.cn: objective 是拉丁形容词 objectivus 的英语形式：object- 加 -ive。词根在 ob-“在前”与 iacere“投”里，也是 subject、adjective、object 的共同来源。

latinIntro.en: Latin objectum 'thing put before' is the neuter noun from obicere; objectivus was used by Duns Scotus. The same iacere also builds subjectum 'thrown under' and adiectivus 'thrown to'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 objectum“被摆到前面之物”是 obicere 的中性名词；objectivus 由邓斯·司各脱使用。同一个 iacere 还构成 subjectum“投在下面”和 adiectivus“投向”。

items.meaning: relating to the object; impartial; a goal
items.meaningCN: 与对象相关的；客观的；目标（-ive 构成形容词，也可作名词）
items.example: The review aims to be objective.

items.meaningCN: 客观地；不带偏见地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The team judged the design objectively.
items.exampleCN: 团队客观地评估了这项设计。

items.meaningCN: 客观性；无偏见（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: Journalists are expected to maintain objectivity.

items.meaning: a thing put before the senses; to oppose
items.meaningCN: 物体；对象；反对（ob-“在前”+ iect“投”）
items.example: A strange object lay on the path.
items.exampleCN: 小路上躺着一个奇怪的物体。

items.meaning: a statement thrown against something; disagreement
items.meaningCN: 异议；反对（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The lawyer raised an objection.

items.meaning: to treat as an object or make concrete
items.meaningCN: 使物化；使具体化（-ify 构成动词）
items.example: The advertisement objectifies the people it shows.
items.exampleCN: 这则广告把画面中的人物化了。

items.meaning: the act of treating someone as an object
items.meaningCN: 物化；对象化（-ication 构成名词）
items.example: The essay discusses the objectification of labour.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章讨论劳动的物化。

items.meaning: literally 'thrown to'; a word added to a noun
items.meaningCN: 字面“投向”；形容词（加在名词上的词）
items.example: Choose a precise adjective for the noun.
items.exampleCN: 为这个名词选一个准确的形容词。

items.meaning: literally 'thrown under'; a topic or a grammatical subject
items.meaningCN: 字面“投在下面”；主题；主语
items.example: The subject of the talk was water.

items.meaning: based on personal feeling rather than the object
items.example: Taste in music is subjective.

latinEntries.meaning: relating to an object; existing as an object of thought
latinEntries.meaningCN: 与对象相关的；作为思想对象存在的（邓斯·司各脱用语）

definition_zh: 义务（良心或道德上必须履行的事）；法律义务（法令、合同或规章所规定的作为或不作为）；债务（必须偿付的款项或必须提供的给付）；人情债（受恩之后觉得应当回报的亏欠感）；约束力（誓约、承诺或规则对人的拘束力量）；受托职责（因担任职务而必须尽到的义务）；契据债券（以文书形式承认的付款义务）；被迫感（觉得别无选择、只能去做的心理压力）
definition_en: a binding requirement, whether moral, legal or contractual, that a person is bound to carry out or to pay
core_image: 一根绳子一头系在人的手腕上，另一头系在一张写满条款的纸上，风吹得纸响，绳子始终不松
scene: 公证处的窗口前，一位老人把一份发黄的借据摊在桌上，说当年借钱的人已经去世，他的儿子仍然每年送来利息。The obligation had outlived the man who signed it.
sceneCN: 这里 obligation 指「按字据必须偿付的债务」（第 3 个义项：必须偿付的款项）；句意为这笔债比签字的人活得更久。可辨识物件：发黄的借据、窗口玻璃、红色印章、利息收条；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 义务；法律责任；债务；人情债；约束力；受托职责

forms.label: 形容词（受约束的；承蒙的）

senses.title: A duty felt in conscience
senses.definition: a duty that a person feels bound in conscience to perform, even when no one can compel it
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在良心上觉得必须履行、即使无人能强制也必须做的义务
senses.example: She felt an obligation to tell the family what she had seen.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得有义务把自己看到的事告诉这家人。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to bind, so the word pictures a person tied to a task before any law appears.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「捆绑」，所以这个词描绘的是在法律出现之前，一个人就已经被系在一件事上。

senses.title: A duty imposed by law or contract
senses.titleCN: 法律或合同规定的义务
senses.definition: a requirement that a statute, contract or official rule lays on a person and that can be enforced
senses.definitionCN: 由法令、合同或正式规章加于某人、并且可以被强制执行的作为或不作为要求
senses.example: The lease imposes an obligation to repair the roof by June.
senses.exampleCN: 租约规定了一项在六月前修好屋顶的义务。
senses.why: Once a court can enforce the bond, the image of a rope becomes a legal relation with a remedy.
senses.whyCN: 一旦法院可以强制执行这根绳子，捆绑的图景就变成带有救济手段的法律关系。

senses.title: A debt that must be paid
senses.definition: a sum of money or a service that one is bound to pay or provide to another
senses.definitionCN: 必须向他人偿付的款项，或必须向他人提供的给付
senses.example: The obligation had outlived the man who signed it.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔债比签字的人活得更久。
senses.why: Bonds are most often counted in money, so the general binding became a figure on a ledger.
senses.whyCN: 捆绑最常见于金钱，于是这种一般的约束就变成账本上的一个数字。

senses.title: A debt of gratitude
senses.definition: the sense of owing something back after receiving help or kindness that cannot be repaid in full
senses.definitionCN: 得到帮助或恩惠之后，觉得应当回报、却又无法完全还清的那种亏欠感
senses.example: He stayed to look after the old teacher out of a sense of obligation.
senses.exampleCN: 他留下来照顾那位老教师，是出于一份人情上的亏欠感。
senses.why: Kindness can bind as firmly as a contract, and English uses the same word for both ties.
senses.whyCN: 恩惠能像合同一样把人系住，英语对这两种束缚用了同一个词。

senses.title: The binding force of a promise
senses.titleCN: 誓约与规则具有的约束力
senses.definition: the force that a promise, oath or rule has in holding a person to a stated course of action
senses.definitionCN: 誓约、承诺或规则把一个人固定在既定做法上的那股力量
senses.example: The oath carried an obligation that he could not easily set aside.
senses.exampleCN: 那个誓约带着一种约束力，他无法轻易搁下。
senses.why: Here the noun names not the task but the pull that keeps a person from walking away.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词指的不是任务，而是不让一个人走开的那股拉力。

senses.title: Duties attached to a trust or office
senses.titleCN: 受托或任职所带来的职责
senses.definition: the specific duties that a person must perform because of a post or a trust accepted
senses.definitionCN: 因担任某个职位或接受某项托付而必须履行的具体职责
senses.example: A trustee's obligations include keeping accounts open to inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 受托人的职责包括保存可供查阅的账目。
senses.why: A post adds its own set, so the general bond becomes a list that other people can check.
senses.whyCN: 一个职位自带一整套要求，于是笼统的捆绑变成别人可以核对的清单。

senses.title: A sealed bond or written undertaking
senses.titleCN: 契据形式的债券与承诺书
senses.definition: in law, a written document under seal by which a person binds himself to pay a sum or to perform an act
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上指加盖印章的文书，当事人在其中承诺付款或履行某项行为
senses.example: The estate settled the obligation recorded in the bond.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产管理人清偿了债券上记载的那笔债务。
senses.why: The word once named the paper itself, because the paper was the thing that did the binding.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾经直接指那张纸，因为起捆绑作用的就是那张纸。

senses.title: The felt pressure of having no choice
senses.definition: the state of feeling compelled to act, whether or not one agrees with the act
senses.definitionCN: 觉得不得不做某事的状态，不论自己是否认同这件事
senses.example: He signed the form under obligation, not out of any belief in the scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 他在被迫的情况下签了表格，并不是因为相信这个方案。
senses.why: When the tie is felt from the inside, the noun describes a pressure rather than a duty owed.
senses.whyCN: 当这根绳子从内部被感受到时，这个名词描述的是压力，而不是欠下的义务。

intro.en: Obligation comes from Latin obligare 'to bind, tie up', built on ob- 'towards, against' and ligare 'to bind'. The noun obligatio passed through Old French into English, keeping both the moral and the legal sense.
intro.cn: obligation 来自拉丁 obligare「捆绑、约束」，由 ob-「朝向、对着」与 ligare「绑」构成。名词 obligatio 经古法语进入英语，同时保留了道德与法律两层意思。

items.en: Ligare meant 'to bind, tie'. It also gives ligament and ligature, where the same root names things that fasten; its deeper origin is not established, so any earlier form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: ligare 意为「绑、系」。它同样给出 ligament 与 ligature，同一个词根在两词中指起固定作用的东西；其更深的来源未获证明，凡为其提出的更早形式都属重构形式。

items.en: Ob- 'towards, against' plus ligare formed obligare, 'to bind towards someone', hence to put a person under a duty. The prefix marks the direction of the tie, not its strength.
items.cn: ob-「朝向、对着」加 ligare 构成 obligare，意为「朝某人绑过去」，引申为使某人负上义务。前缀标的是捆绑的方向，而不是力度。

items.en: The noun obligatio named both the act of binding and the bond itself; Roman law used it for a tie that could be enforced by an action.
items.cn: 名词 obligatio 既指捆绑的动作，也指束缚本身；罗马法用它指可以通过诉讼强制执行的约束关系。

items.en: Old French obligation carried the moral sense of a duty and the legal sense of a bond, and English adopted it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 obligation 兼有道德义务与法律债券两层意思，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: English law kept the written-bond sense, and the everyday moral sense grew beside it; obligation to and under an obligation are the modern frames that separate them.
items.cn: 英国法保留了文书债券的义项，日常的道德义在旁边生长；后接表示对象的介词，与「负有义务」这一固定说法，正是今天区分两者的框架。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of ligare and the English date): the link with religion is real but semantic only, since religio is generally explained as re- plus ligare in the sense of binding fast, while ally and alliance come from ad- plus ligare with a different prefix and a different sense, and obligation shares the root with religion without sharing any meaning.
items.cn: 来源不确定（ligare 的更深来源与英语首见年代）：与 religion 的联系确实存在，但只在词根层面，因为 religio 一般被解释为 re- 加 ligare、取「紧紧绑住」之意，而 ally 与 alliance 则出自 ad- 加 ligare，前缀不同、语义也不同；obligation 与 religion 共享词根，却没有任何义项上的关系。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same binding root, each with a different prefix or ending, so the meanings diverge sharply; group two holds nouns that also put a person under a demand, with a different source for that demand.
note.cn: 第一组同出「绑」这个词根，但前缀或词尾各不相同，语义因此分得很开；第二组是同样把人置于某种要求之下的名词，只是要求的来源不同。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to bind someone by law, by duty or by a favour done, and in polite use simply to do someone a kindness.
entries.definitionCN: 这个名词背后的动词：以法律、义务或恩惠把人绑住；在客套用法中则只表示帮某人一个忙。

entries.definition: Made from the noun with the ending -ory, meaning required rather than optional; it describes the requirement, not the person under it.
entries.definitionCN: 由这个名词加表示「具有……性质的」词尾构成，意为强制的而非可选的；它描述要求本身，而不是被要求的人。

entries.definition: Built on ligare with a different stem: it names the band that binds a joint, and the binding here is physical.
entries.definitionCN: 以 ligare 加另一个词干构成：它指把关节绑住的韧带，这里的捆绑是身体上的。

entries.definition: Generally explained as re- plus ligare, 'to bind fast'; it shares the root but has no sense relation to a duty or a debt.
entries.definitionCN: 一般解释为 re- 加 ligare「紧紧绑住」；它与本词共享词根，却与义务、债务没有任何义项关系。

entries.definition: From ad- 'to' plus ligare, 'to bind to one side'; it names a partner joined by agreement, and the prefix, not the root, does the work.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 ad-「向」加 ligare「绑到一边」；它指因约定而结合的伙伴，起作用的是前缀而不是词根。

entries.definition: What a person owes by law, by office or by conscience; duty is the content, while obligation stresses the tie that holds the person to it.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人依法、依职或依良知所欠之事；义务是内容，而 obligation 强调把人系在这件事上的那根绳子。

entries.definition: A promise or engagement a person has taken on, usually by choice; obligation can be imposed without consent.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人通常自愿承担下来的承诺或投入；obligation 则可以在未经同意时被加于身上。

entries.definition: Legal responsibility for a debt or damage, measured in money; it is the narrow financial end of obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 对债务或损害承担的法律责任，以金钱衡量；它是 obligation 最窄的财务一端。

entries.definition: A condition that must be met, often written into a rule or a contract; it names the condition, not the bond that makes it binding.
entries.definitionCN: 必须满足的条件，常写入规则或合同；它指条件本身，而不是使其具有约束力的那根绳子。

entries.definition: The state of having to answer for something; it looks at who must explain, while obligation looks at what binds them to act.
entries.definitionCN: 必须为某事作出交代的状态；它着眼的是该由谁解释，而 obligation 着眼的是把人绑向行动的东西。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb of binding, its prefix, the real family, the real phrases, and the relatives that share the root but carry different prefixes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「捆绑」动词、它的前缀、真实的词族、真实的搭配，以及共享词根却带不同前缀的亲戚。

normal.en: Ob- means towards and ligare means to bind, so an obligation is a rope tied towards a task.
normal.cn: ob- 意为「朝向」，ligare 意为「绑」，所以义务就是一根朝某件事绑过去的绳子。

normal.en: The family runs oblige, obliged, obliging, obligatory, obligatorily and obligee.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 oblige、obliged、obliging、obligatory、obligatorily 与 obligee。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the frames: a legal obligation, under an obligation to, fulfil an obligation, without obligation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出常用框架：法律义务、有义务去做、履行义务、不附带义务。

normal.en: The same root appears with other prefixes: a ligament binds a joint, religion binds fast, and an ally is bound to one side.
normal.cn: 同一个词根配上别的前缀：ligament 绑住关节，religion 取「紧紧绑住」之意，ally 则是被绑到一边的伙伴。

normal.en: Obligation is what ties a person to act; responsibility is what a person must answer for afterwards.
normal.cn: obligation 是把人绑向行动的东西，responsibility 则是事后必须为之作答的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a rope running from a wrist to a sheet of clauses, slack enough to move but never loose enough to slip off.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子从手腕连到一页条款上，松到可以活动，却绝不会松脱。

abstract.en: Picture a signed card in a coat pocket that grows heavier with every year it is carried.
abstract.cn: 想象外套口袋里一张签过字的卡片，带得越久就越沉。

abstract.en: Picture two posts with a rope stretched between them, so that walking past means ducking under it.
abstract.cn: 想象两根柱子之间拉着一根绳，走过那里就得低头钻过去。

examples.en: Members are under an obligation to declare any outside income.
examples.cn: 成员有义务申报任何外部收入。

examples.en: He helped her move, and she now feels an obligation to return the favour.
examples.cn: 他帮她搬了家，她现在觉得欠着一份应当回报的人情。

examples.en: The bond is an obligation enforceable in court.
examples.cn: 这张债券是一项可以在法院强制执行的义务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝向 + 绑」——把你朝某件事绑过去的那根绳子，就是义务；绳子换成钱，就是债务

root: 拉丁 obligare「捆绑、约束」= ob-（朝向、对着）+ ligare「绑」；名词 obligatio 经古法语 obligation 进入英语。同根词有 ligament、ligature、religion（re- 加 ligare，紧紧绑住）、ally 与 alliance（ad- 加 ligare）；前缀不同，语义各异。ligare 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rope: conscience ties it, law tightens it, money counts it, gratitude feels it, the noun then names the force itself, lists the duties of a post, records it as a sealed bond, and finally describes the pressure of being pulled from inside.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一根绳子展开：良心先把它系上，法律把它收紧，金钱把它算成数目，感恩从内部感到它；随后名词指这股力量本身、列出职位的职责、把它记成盖章的债券，最后描述被从内部拉扯的压力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope from a wrist to a page of clauses, slack enough to move but never loose enough to slip off.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根从手腕连到条款纸页的绳子，松到可以活动，却绝不会松脱。

branches.en: INNER TIE AND ITS FORCE: the duty felt and the binding power that holds a person are one rope seen as content and as strength.
branches.cn: 内在的系与它的力：被感受到的义务与把人固定的力量，是同一根绳子作为内容与作为力度的一面。

branches.en: PAPER AND LAW: a statute and a sealed bond are two ways of writing the tie down.
branches.cn: 纸与法：法令与盖章债券，是把这根绳子写下来的两种方式。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF DEBT: money can be counted and repaid, while gratitude cannot.
branches.cn: 两种债：钱可以算清也可以还清，恩情却不行。

branches.en: THE POST: an office supplies its own list of duties, which other people can inspect.
branches.cn: 职位：一个岗位自带一份职责清单，别人可以逐项核对。

branches.en: PULLED FROM INSIDE: when the rope is felt rather than owed, the word names compulsion.
branches.cn: 从内部被拉：当绳子是被感受到而不是被欠下时，这个词指的就是被迫。

intro.en: Obligation reads as a prefix of direction, a root meaning to bind, and a noun ending that names the resulting state or instrument.
intro.cn: obligation 可以读成表示方向的前缀、意为「绑」的词根，以及指称由此形成的状态或文书的名称词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root ligare also gives ligament, ligature, religion, ally and alliance; ob- marks direction towards, while re- and ad- give those other words their different senses.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 ligare 还给出 ligament、ligature、religion、ally 与 alliance；ob- 标出「朝向」，re- 与 ad- 则让其余各词各有不同语义。

items.example: The prefix shows the direction in which the binding is done.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀指出捆绑是朝哪个方向做的。

items.example: The root supplies the physical picture of a rope.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供绳子的具体形象。

items.meaning: to bind towards; to put under a duty
items.example: The verb turns a literal rope into a duty owed to a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把字面的绳子变成对某人的义务。

items.example: The Latin noun names both the act and the tie it creates.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词既指动作，也指动作造成的束缚。

items.meaning: a duty; a debt; a bond
items.example: The obligation had outlived the man who signed it.
items.exampleCN: 这笔债比签字的人活得更久。

items.example: Attendance at the safety briefing is obligatory.
items.exampleCN: 参加安全说明会是强制性的。

items.meaning: to bind by duty; to do a kindness
items.example: The rules oblige the carrier to inspect every crate.
items.exampleCN: 规则要求承运方检查每一个板条箱。

items.meaning: the person to whom a bond is owed
items.example: The obligee may demand payment on the stated date.
items.exampleCN: 债权人可以在约定日期要求付款。

definition_zh: 迫使；使不得不；施恩于；帮……的忙；应允；效劳；感激；感谢
definition_en: to force someone to do something by law, duty or circumstance; also to do someone a favour, to comply with a request, and to be grateful for a kindness
core_image: 一根看不见的绳子把人牵向唯一的选择，绳子的另一头却系着一份人情
scene: 暴雨冲垮了唯一的渡口，赶路的人被困在河岸上，前后都没有别的路可走。The flooded river obliged the travellers to wait for a boat.
sceneCN: 这里是「迫使、使不得不」（第 1 个义项：因法律、职责或形势而不得不做）；句意为暴涨的河水逼得行人只能等船。可辨物件：浑黄的河水、岸边的行囊、断掉的木桥。

pos.zh: 迫使；使负有义务；施恩于

collocations.zh: 非常感谢（旧式客气说法）

derivatives.zh: 由 oblige 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「义务；责任；债务」
由 oblige 的词干加 -atory 构成，义为「必须的；强制的」
由 oblige 加 -ing 构成，义为「乐于助人的；殷勤的」
由 obliging 加 -ly 构成，义为「殷勤地；乐意地」

senses.title: To force someone by law, duty or circumstances
senses.definition: to make someone do something because of a law, a duty or the pressure of events
senses.definitionCN: 因法律、职责或形势的压力而使人不得不做某事
senses.example: Heavy snow obliged the climbers to turn back.
senses.exampleCN: 大雪迫使登山者折返。
senses.why: The Latin verb obligare meant to bind up, and a law or a storm acts like a rope that leaves a person only one course of action.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obligare 本义是「捆住」，法律、职责或一场暴风雪都像绳子一样把人拴在唯一的选择上，于是有了「迫使」。

senses.title: To do someone a service or favour
senses.definition: to help someone by doing what they have asked, as a favour
senses.definitionCN: 按对方的请求出力，作为一种好意
senses.example: Our host obliged us with a lift to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 主人开车送我们去了车站。
senses.why: A kindness puts the receiver in the giver's debt, so the verb for binding also came to mean laying a soft obligation of gratitude on someone.
senses.whyCN: 一份好意让受助者欠下人情，于是那个表示「捆住」的动词，转而指用善意把对方轻轻系在自己这一边。

senses.title: To comply with a request; willing to help
senses.definition: to do what someone has asked, often willingly and without any pressure
senses.definitionCN: 按别人的请求去做，往往是自愿的、没有压力的
senses.example: The shop assistant obliged when I asked for another size.
senses.exampleCN: 我请店员换一个尺码，她很爽快地答应了。
senses.why: Here the bond is chosen rather than imposed: the helper ties his own action to another person's request, and the adjective obliging names that temperament.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「捆」不是被强加的，而是自己选的：帮忙的人把自己的行动系在别人的请求上，形容词 obliging 正形容这种性情。

senses.title: To be grateful for a favour received
senses.definition: used in the phrase be obliged to someone, meaning to be thankful for a kindness
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be obliged to 这一说法，表示因受恩惠而心存感谢
senses.example: I am much obliged to you for your help.
senses.exampleCN: 承蒙相助，我不胜感激。
senses.why: A favour leaves the receiver bound to the giver, and English turned that bond into a polite formula of thanks.
senses.whyCN: 受了恩惠的人觉得自己欠着对方，英语就把这条人情之绳固化成客气的致谢说法，be obliged to 由此表示感激。

intro.en: Oblige comes from a Latin verb that literally means to bind, and that rope shows up in every one of its senses.
intro.cn: oblige 来自一个字面意思为「捆绑」的拉丁动词，而这条绳子出现在它的每一个义项里。

items.en: Ligare meant to tie or bind, and it stands behind ligament and the whole family of words about obligation.
items.cn: ligare 意为捆绑、系住，是 ligament 以及整个「义务」词族的共同词根。

items.en: The prefix ob- joined ligare to make obligare, to bind up or fasten, and then to bind a person by promise or duty.
items.cn: 前缀 ob- 与 ligare 合成 obligare，本义是把东西捆好、扎紧，再引申为用承诺或职责把人约束住。

items.en: Old French obliger kept both jobs: to bind someone by a pledge and, by extension, to lay a kindness on someone.
items.cn: 古法语 obliger 同时保留两种用法：用誓言约束某人，以及引申为把一份好意施加于某人。

items.en: English borrowed the verb for moral and legal binding, then for the favour that puts another in one's debt.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，先指道德与法律上的约束，再指那种让受助者欠下人情的帮忙。

items.en: Modern English keeps the force sense as the main one, while the polite phrase much obliged survives as a formal thank-you.
items.cn: 现代英语以「迫使」为主要义项，而客气话 much obliged 作为正式的致谢一直沿用至今。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives built on the Latin root for binding; the near-meaning group collects words for compulsion and for gratitude.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在「捆绑」这一拉丁词根上的同族词，近义组收表示强制与感激的词。

entries.definition: Willing to help and quick to do favours.

entries.definition: Feeling thankful for something received.

normalIntro.en: The word is a rope in disguise: ligare means to bind, and each sense shows a different kind of tie.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词其实是一条化装的绳子：ligare 意为捆绑，每个义项都呈现一种不同的系法。

normal.en: The core of obligare is ligare, to bind, so oblige starts as the act of tying a person to a duty.
normal.cn: obligare 的核心是 ligare（捆绑），所以 oblige 一开始就是把一个人拴在责任上的动作。

normal.en: Obligation adds -ation to the verb and names the rope itself: the duty that holds a person.
normal.cn: obligation 在动词后加 -ation，指的是绳子本身，也就是约束人的那份义务。

normal.en: Obliging drops the force and keeps only the willingness, which is why it means helpful.
normal.cn: obliging 去掉了强制，只留下自愿，因此表示「乐于助人的」。

normal.en: Much obliged is a polite way of saying that kindness has bound you to the other person.
normal.cn: much obliged 是一种客气说法，意思是对方的善意把你系住了。

normal.en: Noblesse oblige joins the word with nobility: high rank brings duties rather than privileges.
normal.cn: noblesse oblige 把这个词与贵族相连：高地位带来的是责任，而不是特权。

abstract.en: Picture one rope that is now a law, now a storm, now a favour.
abstract.cn: 想象同一根绳子，一会儿是法律，一会儿是暴风雪，一会儿是一份好意。

abstract.en: The same word can push and can thank, because both are ways of being tied to another person.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能推人向前，也能道谢，因为两者都是被系在别人身上的方式。

abstract.en: A favour is a soft rope: nobody forces you, yet you still feel the pull.
abstract.cn: 好意是一根柔软的绳子：没人强迫你，你仍然感到那股拉力。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bond; the senses divide into being bound by law or circumstance, binding another by kindness, willingly accepting a request, and thanking the one who bound you.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「捆绑」；义项分成被法律或形势拴住、用善意系住别人、自愿应承请求，以及向系住自己的人道谢。

core.cn: 核心意象：一根看不见的绳子把人牵向唯一的选择，绳子的另一端还系着一份人情。

definition_zh: 观察；观测；观察结果；评论；（对规则的）遵守
definition_en: the act of watching something carefully, a recorded result of such watching, or a remark based on it
core_image: 一个人站在窗前，手里拿着本子，把鸟落下的时间一秒一秒写下来。
scene: 医生让病人先留院一晚，第二天早上再看检查数据。The patient stayed in the hospital for a night of observation.
sceneCN: 这里 observation 是“医学上的观察期、留观”（第 4 个义项）；句意：病人留院接受一晚的观察；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 观察；观测；观察结果；评论；遵守

senses.title: Watching with attention
senses.definition: the act of watching someone or something closely and with attention
senses.definitionCN: 密切而专注地注视某人或某事的行为
senses.example: Careful observation showed that the birds returned at the same hour each day.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细观察显示，这些鸟每天在同一时刻返回。
senses.why: Observation is not passive seeing: the watcher has chosen an object and a purpose, so attention is the defining element.
senses.whyCN: 观察不是被动地看见：观察者已经选定了对象与目的，因此“专注”才是定义性的要素。

senses.title: A recorded result
senses.titleCN: 观察结果：本子上那行字
senses.definition: a piece of information obtained by watching and often written down for later use
senses.definitionCN: 通过观察获得、常被记录下来备用的信息
senses.example: The notebook contained observations from six mornings at the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 笔记本里记着六个早晨在湖边的观察结果。
senses.why: Once written, the act becomes a fact others can read; the word then names the record rather than the watching.
senses.whyCN: 一旦写下来，行为就变成别人可读的事实；此时这个词命名的是记录，而不是“看”本身。

senses.title: A remark drawn from noticing
senses.definition: a spoken or written remark based on something noticed
senses.definitionCN: 基于所注意到的事情而作出的口头或书面评论
senses.example: His observation that the room felt colder was correct.
senses.exampleCN: 他说房间变冷了，这个观察是对的。
senses.why: The sense shifts from the eye to the mouth: a remark is called an observation when it reports a noticed fact rather than an opinion.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项从眼睛移到嘴：当一句话报告的是被注意到的事实而非意见时，它就被称作 observation。

senses.title: A medical watch
senses.titleCN: 留观：先看着，等数据说话
senses.definition: a period during which a patient is watched in hospital before a decision is made
senses.definitionCN: 病人留院接受看护、等待作出决定的一段时间
senses.example: She was kept in observation overnight after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 摔倒后她被留院观察了一夜。
senses.why: Medicine uses observation as a treatment stage: when the diagnosis is still open, watching is safer than acting.
senses.whyCN: 医学把观察当作一个治疗阶段：诊断尚未确定时，看着比动手更安全。

senses.title: Keeping a rule
senses.titleCN: 遵守：把规定看在眼里并照做
senses.definition: the keeping or honouring of a law, custom, or religious practice
senses.definitionCN: 遵守或尊重法律、习俗或宗教实践
senses.example: Observation of the Sabbath was strict in that community.
senses.exampleCN: 那个社群对安息日的遵守很严格。
senses.why: The older sense of observare is to heed or keep; the same verb that means watch over also means keep faith with a rule.
senses.whyCN: observare 更早的含义是“留意、守护”；同一个既表示“看护”又表示“守信于规则”的动词。

senses.title: A post for watching
senses.titleCN: 观察位：专门用来盯的地方
senses.definition: a place, especially a military one, set up for watching an area
senses.definitionCN: 为监视某一区域而设置的场所，尤指军事用途
senses.example: The soldiers held the observation post on the ridge through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们整夜守住山脊上的观察哨。
senses.why: The act needs a place; when watching is continuous, the place itself takes the name and becomes part of the operation.
senses.whyCN: 观察需要地点；当观察持续进行时，地点本身也取了这个名字，成为行动的一部分。

senses.title: Studying from inside a group
senses.titleCN: 参与式观察：进去，同时记下来
senses.definition: a research method in which the researcher joins a group and records its life while taking part in it
senses.definitionCN: 研究者加入某群体、在参与其生活的同时作记录的研究方法
senses.example: Her participant observation of the night market lasted a full year.
senses.exampleCN: 她对夜市的参与式观察持续了整整一年。
senses.why: The method accepts a tension: to see ordinary life closely one must enter it, yet entering changes what is being observed.
senses.whyCN: 这种方法接受一种张力：要贴近看日常生活就必须进去，可一旦进去，被观察的对象也变了。

senses.title: Measuring the sky
senses.titleCN: 天文观测：把望远镜对准天上
senses.definition: the systematic recording of celestial objects and events with instruments
senses.definitionCN: 用仪器对天体与天象作系统记录
senses.example: The observation of the eclipse required clear skies and an exact location.
senses.exampleCN: 观测这次日食需要晴朗天空和精确地点。
senses.why: Astronomy turns observation into data: the eye is replaced by a detector, and the record must state time, place, and instrument.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把观察变成数据：眼睛被探测器取代，记录必须写明时间、地点与仪器。

intro.en: Observation comes from Latin observatio, a watching or a heed, from observare: ob- 'over, before' plus servare 'to keep, watch over'. Servare also gives preserve, reserve, and conserve.
intro.cn: observation 来自拉丁语 observatio“看护、留意”，出自 observare：ob-“在上、在前”加 servare“守护、留意”。servare 还给出 preserve、reserve、conserve。

items.en: Servare meant to keep, guard, or preserve. The idea of keeping is older than the idea of looking.
items.cn: servare 意为保持、守护、保存。“守”的观念比“看”的观念更早。

items.en: Ob- added the sense of direction or attention: to watch over, to heed, to keep a rule, and to observe signs.
items.cn: ob- 增加了方向与注意的含义：看护、留意、遵守规则，以及观察征兆。

items.en: The noun covered watching, noting, and also compliance with a custom or a law.
items.cn: 该名词涵盖看护、记录，也涵盖对习俗或法律的遵守。

items.en: French kept both the watching sense and the remark sense, and English borrowed both in the 14th century.
items.cn: 法语同时保留了“观察”与“评论”两义，英语于 14 世纪把两者一并借入。

items.en: English observation grew in science and navigation, where watching had to be recorded with time and place.
items.cn: 英语 observation 在科学与航海领域壮大，那里的观察必须连同时间与地点一起记录。

items.en: The 19th and 20th centuries added medical observation, participant observation, and instrument-based astronomical observation.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪增加了医学留观、参与式观察，以及依靠仪器的天文观测。

note.en: The first group is the observe family; the second compares ways of gaining knowledge by watching, checking, or testing.
note.cn: 第一组是 observe 词族；第二组比较通过观看、核查或检验获取知识的几种方式。

entries.definition: to watch carefully, to notice, or to keep a rule. It names the action behind observation.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细观察、注意到，或遵守规则；命名的是 observation 背后的动作。

entries.definition: a person who watches, especially one sent to report on an event.
entries.definitionCN: 观察的人，尤指被派去报道某一事件的人。

entries.definition: quick to notice things; also careful to keep a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 善于注意细节的；也指谨慎守规的。

entries.definition: the keeping of a law, rite, or custom. It is the 'compliance' sense without the scientific one.
entries.definitionCN: 对法律、仪式或习俗的遵守；只有“遵从”义，没有科学观察义。

entries.definition: looking at something over time, often without a formal purpose. Observation adds method.
entries.definitionCN: 持续地看，常无正式目的；observation 则增加了方法。

entries.definition: continuous checking by instruments or staff, usually against limits. It is observation with a threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 用仪器或人员持续核查，通常对照限值；是有阈值的观察。

entries.definition: the assignment of a number to a property. It turns observation into quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 给性质赋予数值；它把观察变成数量。

entries.definition: something said briefly. It need not be based on careful watching.
entries.definitionCN: 简短说出的话；不必基于仔细的观察。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ob- 'over' plus servare 'keep'. Observation is keeping watch, and keeping a rule.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ob-“在上”加 servare“守护”。observation 就是守望着，也是守着规则。

normal.en: Observe means both to watch and to keep: the same act of holding something in view.
normal.cn: observe 既表示“看”，也表示“守”：都是把某物保持在视野里。

normal.en: An observation notebook is a watch that leaves a mark.
normal.cn: 观察笔记本就是一只会留下痕迹的表。

normal.en: In hospital, observation is a room where time does the testing.
normal.cn: 在医院，observation 是一间让时间来检验的病房。

normal.en: An observation post is the act of watching with a fixed address.
normal.cn: 观察哨就是有了固定地址的“看”。

normal.en: Astronomers write down three things: what, when, and with which instrument.
normal.cn: 天文学家记三件事：看到了什么、什么时候、用什么仪器。

abstract.en: Observation never arrives pure; the choice of what to watch is already a theory about what matters.
abstract.cn: 观察从不以纯粹状态到来；选择看什么，本身已是关于“什么重要”的理论。

abstract.en: The same verb means to watch and to obey, as if attention and loyalty came from one root.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词既表示观看又表示服从，仿佛注意与忠诚出自同一根。

abstract.en: To observe a group closely is to change it; the observer is always part of the observed world.
abstract.cn: 近距离观察一个群体就会改变它；观察者永远是被观察世界的一部分。

examples.en: The ornithologist's observation of the nest lasted from dawn until the chicks fledged.
examples.cn: 这位鸟类学家对鸟巢的观察从黎明持续到雏鸟长出飞羽。

examples.en: After the head injury, the patient stayed under observation for twenty-four hours.
examples.cn: 头部受伤后，病人留院观察了二十四小时。

examples.en: Her observation that the machine ran quieter after warming up turned out to be important.
examples.cn: 她观察到机器预热后运转更安静，后来证明这一点很重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: observe（观察）+ ation（名词）——看得很仔细，还记下来，就是观察、观测。

root: 源自拉丁语 observatio（看护、留意、遵从），出自 observare：ob-“在上、在前”加 servare“守护、保持”。同一词根兼有“看”与“守”两面，因此既指观察、观测，也指对规则、习俗的遵守。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of observation, all descended from one act of keeping watch. The watch can be scientific, medical, military, or social; its product can be a record, a remark, a data set, or a habit of obeying.
sensesIntro.cn: observation 的八个义项都源自同一个“守望”动作。守望可以是科学的、医学的、军事的或社会的；其产物可以是记录、评论、数据集，或遵守的习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a window with a notebook, writing down the exact second a bird lands.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗边的人拿着本子，记下鸟落下的那一秒。

chain: LATIN OBSERVARE TO WATCH OVER HEED
LATIN OBSERVATIO A WATCHING A HEEDING
ITS RECORD ITS REMARK ITS POST ITS METHOD

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS RECORD: watching with purpose, and the line written down afterwards.
branches.cn: 行为与记录：有目的地看，以及随后写下的那一行。

branches.en: WORD AND RULE: a remark drawn from noticing, and the keeping of a law or custom.
branches.cn: 言语与规则：由注意得出的评论，以及对法律或习俗的遵守。

branches.en: MEDICAL WAITING: a patient watched until the evidence becomes clear.
branches.cn: 医学等待：病人被观察到证据明朗为止。

branches.en: PLACE AND METHOD: a post built for watching, and a researcher watching from inside a group.
branches.cn: 地点与方法：为观察而建的哨位，以及研究者从群体内部观察。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTAL WATCHING: the sky recorded with time, place, and detector.
branches.cn: 仪器化观察：连同时间、地点与探测器一起记录天空。

intro.en: Observation is observe plus -ation, the action-noun suffix. The family adds -er for the person, -ant for the habit, -ance for the keeping of a rule, and -able for what can be seen.
intro.cn: observation 是 observe 加 -ation（动作名词后缀）。词族用 -er 表示人，-ant 表示习性，-ance 表示对规则的遵守，-able 表示可被看见。

latinIntro.en: The base is servare, to keep or guard, with ob- adding the direction of attention. Related Latin words give preserve, reserve, conserve, and servant.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 servare“保持、守护”，ob- 增加注意的方向。相关拉丁词给出 preserve、reserve、conserve、servant。

items.meaning: to watch closely, notice, or keep a rule
items.example: Scientists observe the same plot every spring.
items.exampleCN: 科学家每年春天观察同一块样地。

items.meaning: the act, result, or remark of watching
items.meaningCN: 观察的行为、结果或评论
items.example: His observation was recorded in the margin.
An observer sat at the back of the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 一名观察员坐在会议后排。

items.meaning: quick to notice; careful to comply
items.meaningCN: 善于察觉的；谨慎遵守的
items.example: An observant reader will spot the repeated date.
items.exampleCN: 细心的读者会注意到重复出现的日期。

items.meaning: the keeping of a law, rite, or custom
items.meaningCN: 对法律、仪式或习俗的遵守
items.example: Observance of the treaty was monitored by neutrals.
items.exampleCN: 条约的遵守情况由中立国监督。

items.meaning: able to be seen or noticed
items.example: The effect is observable only at low temperatures.
items.exampleCN: 这一效应只在低温下可观察到。

items.meaning: a place built for watching the sky or nature
items.meaningCN: 为观测天空或自然而建的场所；天文台
items.example: The observatory opens to the public on Fridays.
items.exampleCN: 这座天文台周五向公众开放。

items.meaning: to keep something safe from harm or change
items.meaningCN: 保护某物免受损害或改变；保存
items.example: The salt preserves the fish for the winter.

items.meaning: to keep back for later use
items.example: They reserved two seats near the window.
items.exampleCN: 他们预留了两个靠窗座位。

items.meaning: to keep from being lost or wasted
items.example: The town conserves water during dry summers.
items.exampleCN: 这个镇在干旱夏季节约用水。

latinEntries.meaning: to watch over, heed, comply with
a watching, a remark, a compliance

definition_zh: 观察；注意到；作科学观测；评论说；遵守；庆祝（节日或仪式）
definition_en: to watch something carefully, to notice, to make a scientific observation, to remark, or to keep a rule or mark a day
core_image: 山顶观测台上，一个人屏住呼吸把望远镜对准同一颗星，每隔一刻钟记下一次位置
scene: 山顶的观测台上，一个人每隔一刻钟记录一次那颗星的位置，直到云层压过来。Astronomers observe the same star for months to fix its distance.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：为获取信息而长时间仔细观看；句意为天文学家连续数月观测同一颗星，以确定它的距离。图中可辨识物件：望远镜、记录表、计时器、星图；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 观察；注意到；观测；评论；遵守；庆祝

senses.title: To watch with full attention
senses.definition: to watch someone or something closely over time in order to learn how it behaves
senses.definitionCN: 为弄清某人或某物的行为而长时间仔细观看
senses.example: Astronomers observe the same star for months to fix its distance.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家连续数月观测同一颗星，以确定它的距离。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to watch over and heed, so sustained attention rather than a glance is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为看守并留心，因此持续注意而非一眼扫过，是最古老的一层。

senses.title: To notice
senses.definition: to see or become aware of something, often without looking for it
senses.definitionCN: 看见或意识到某物，往往并非刻意寻找
senses.example: I observed a crack in the glass before it fell.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃掉落之前，我就注意到上面有道裂痕。
senses.why: Attention can be caught as well as directed, so the same verb covers the moment something enters the eye.
senses.whyCN: 注意力既能被引导也能被抓住，因此同一个动词也覆盖某物进入视野的那一刻。

senses.title: To measure in a study
senses.definition: to record a phenomenon under controlled conditions as part of scientific work
senses.definitionCN: 作为科研工作的一部分，在受控条件下记录一种现象
senses.example: The team observe the cells every six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 团队每六小时观察一次这些细胞。
senses.why: Measurement begins with watching, and science made the watching formal by giving it conditions and records.
senses.whyCN: 测量始于观看，而科学通过附加条件与记录，把观看变得正式。

senses.title: To remark
senses.definition: to say something as a comment on what has been noticed
senses.definitionCN: 就注意到的事情说一句话作为评论
senses.example: The reviewer observed that the sample was too small.
senses.exampleCN: 评审人评论说样本太小。
senses.why: A remark is often the spoken form of something noticed, so the verb moved from the eye to the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 评论常常是「注意到的东西」的口头形式，这个动词于是从眼睛移到了嘴。

senses.title: To keep a rule
senses.definition: to act in accordance with a law, rule, custom or promise
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律、规则、习俗或承诺行事
senses.example: Drivers must observe the speed limit near the school.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在学校附近必须遵守限速。
senses.why: To observe a rule is to keep watch over yourself, the same inward attention the Latin verb first described.
senses.whyCN: 遵守规则就是看住自己，正是那个拉丁动词最初描述的内在注意。

senses.title: To mark a day or rite
senses.definition: to celebrate or carry out a day, festival or ceremony in the proper way
senses.definitionCN: 以适当方式庆祝某个日子、节日或举行仪式
senses.example: The village observes the harvest festival every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子每年秋天都过丰收节。
senses.why: A custom is kept by being performed on its day, so the sense of keeping widened to the act of celebration.
senses.whyCN: 习俗靠在其日子被践行而得以保持，因此「持守」之义扩展到庆祝行为。

senses.title: To keep someone under watch
senses.definition: to watch a person or place secretly, especially as part of an investigation
senses.definitionCN: 暗中监视某人或某地，尤作为调查的一部分
senses.example: Police observe the house from a van across the street.
senses.exampleCN: 警察在街对面的货车里监视那栋房子。
senses.why: The same careful watching turns into surveillance when the watcher does not wish to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 当观看者不愿被看见，同样的仔细观看就变成了监视。

senses.title: To watch without interfering
senses.definition: in research, to study behaviour while taking no part that would change it
senses.definitionCN: 在研究中研究行为，同时不介入以免改变它
senses.example: The psychologist observes the class from the back of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学家在教室后排观察这个班。
senses.why: If the observer changes what is observed, the record is spoiled, so method demands watching with hands off.
senses.whyCN: 观察者若改变了被观察对象，记录就毁了，因此方法要求袖手旁观。

intro.en: Observe comes from Latin observare 'to watch over, heed', built on ob- 'over, before' and servare 'to keep, preserve'. The rule-keeping and celebration senses came through religious usage, and the scientific sense settled in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: observe 来自拉丁语 observare「看守、留心」，由 ob-「在……之上、在……之前」与 servare「保持、守护」构成。守规与庆祝两义经宗教用法而来，科学观测义则在十七世纪定型。

items.en: Servare meant to keep safe, preserve or watch over, and it stands behind preserve, reserve and conserve.
items.cn: servare 意为保全、守护、看守，preserve、reserve 与 conserve 都出自它。

items.en: The similar-looking servire meant to serve, and it gave servant and service; the two Latin verbs are different words.
items.cn: 形近的 servire 意为服侍，产生了 servant 与 service；这两个拉丁动词是不同的词。

items.en: Ob- plus servare made a verb for watching over something and attending to it, with attention as the core.
items.cn: ob- 加 servare 构成「看守并留心某物」的动词，核心在注意。

items.en: Old French observer carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of keeping a rule.
items.cn: 古法语 observer 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，最初意为遵守规则。

items.en: Observing the Sabbath and observing a fast fixed the senses of keeping a custom and of celebrating its day.
items.cn: 守安息日、守斋期固定了「持守习俗」与「在其日子举行」两种含义。

items.en: Seventeenth-century astronomy made observe a technical word for recorded watching, and observatory and observer followed.
items.cn: 十七世纪的天文学把 observe 变成指「有记录观看」的技术词，天文台与观察者二词随之而来。

note.en: The first group shares the keeping root or looks close; the second group names ways of watching.
note.cn: 第一组共享「守护」词根或形近；第二组是各种「看」的方式。

entries.definition: The act or result of watching and recording.
entries.definitionCN: 观看并记录的行为或结果。

entries.definition: The person who watches, including the mere onlooker.
entries.definitionCN: 进行观看的人，也包括单纯旁观者。

entries.definition: Quick to notice details; also careful in keeping rules.
entries.definitionCN: 善于察觉细节的；也指守规谨慎的。

entries.definition: The keeping of a rule or rite, not the act of looking.
entries.definitionCN: 对规则或仪式的遵行，而非观看动作。

entries.definition: A building fitted for watching the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 为观测天空而建的场所。

entries.definition: To keep safe from harm, from the same keeping verb with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 使免受损害，同一守护动词加不同前缀。

entries.definition: Work done for others, from servire 'to serve', not from servare.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人所做的工作，出自表示「服侍」的拉丁动词，而非表示「守护」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: The everyday word for looking at something over a period, with less formality.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指持续一段时间看某物，正式程度较低。

entries.definition: To become aware of something, without the suggestion of sustained study.
entries.definitionCN: 意识到某物，不含持续研究的意味。

entries.definition: To keep a continuous check, often with instruments.
entries.definitionCN: 持续检查，常借助仪器。

entries.definition: To look over a whole area or group, often to record its state.
entries.definitionCN: 遍览整个区域或群体，常为记录其状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the keeping verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of rules, rites and research.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「守护」动词、真实同族词，以及规则、仪式与研究里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin servare meant to keep safe, so observe is literally to keep watch over something.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 servare 意为保全，observe 字面就是看住某物。

normal.en: The family runs observe, observation, observer, observant and observatory.
normal.cn: 同族词有 observe、observation、observer、observant 与 observatory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: observe a rule, observe a holiday, observe that.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：遵守规则、庆祝节日、评论说。

normal.en: Preserve and reserve share the keeping verb, while servant and service come from the serving verb.
normal.cn: preserve 与 reserve 共享「守护」动词，而 servant 与 service 出自「服侍」动词。

normal.en: An observatory is a building named for the watching, not for the stars.
normal.cn: 天文台是因「观看」而得名，而非因星星。

abstract.en: To observe a rule is to watch yourself as closely as you watch others.
abstract.cn: 遵守规则，就是像看别人那样看住自己。

abstract.en: The observer who changes the scene has already lost the thing worth recording.
abstract.cn: 改变场景的观察者，已经失去了值得记录的东西。

abstract.en: Attention is the whole word: watch, keep, and do not blink.
abstract.cn: 整个词就是注意：看着、守着、别眨眼。

examples.en: She observed the birds from the hide without making a sound.
examples.cn: 她藏在小棚里观察鸟，没有发出一点声音。

examples.en: Every driver must observe the signs at the crossing.
examples.cn: 每位司机在路口都必须遵守标志。

examples.en: The committee observed a minute of silence for the victims.
examples.cn: 委员会为遇难者默哀一分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「欧布泽夫」——守在旁边盯住不放，看到什么就记下来：观察

root: 拉丁语 servare「保全、守护」→ observare「看守、留心」（ob- 加 servare）；经古法语 observer 进入英语。守规与庆祝义经宗教用法而来，科学观测义在十七世纪定型。注意与 servire「服侍」并非同词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pair of watching eyes: sustained attention, a sudden notice, a measured record, a spoken remark, a rule kept, a festival marked, a house watched in secret, and a class studied without interference.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一双观看的眼睛：持续注意、忽然察觉、有记录的测量、口头评论、被遵守的规则、被举行的节日、被暗中监视的房子，以及不干预地研究的课堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: on a hilltop a watcher holds a telescope on one star and writes its position every quarter hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：山顶的观测者用望远镜对准一颗星，每刻钟记下它的位置。

branches.en: THE EYES: watching for a long time, and catching something in passing.
branches.cn: 那双眼：长时间的看，与路过时捕捉到什么。

branches.en: THE RECORD: cells counted every six hours, a class watched from the back without interference.
branches.cn: 记录：每六小时数一次细胞，在教室后排不干预地观察一个班。

branches.en: THE MOUTH: a note spoken aloud after the eyes have done their work.
branches.cn: 嘴：眼睛做完活之后，说出口的一句评论。

branches.en: THE KEPT RULE: attention turned inward, so that the driver watches himself.
branches.cn: 被守的规则：注意转向内部，司机看住自己。

branches.en: THE MARKED DAY AND THE SECRET WATCH: a rite performed on its date, a house watched from a van.
branches.cn: 被举行的日子与暗中监视：在正日子举行的仪式，与从货车里盯住的房子。

intro.en: Observe is a Latin verb of keeping watch, and its family split off from the separate verb meaning to serve.
intro.cn: observe 是一个表示看守的拉丁动词，其词族与另一个意为服侍的动词分道而行。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is servare, ob-, observare and the noun observatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 servare、ob-、observare 与名词 observatio。

items.example: The verb keeps the image of a guard at a post.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留着岗哨看守的意象。

items.example: It also gives preserve, reserve and conserve.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「保存」「保留」与「保护」三词的来源。

items.example: It gives servant and service, and is not the root here.
items.exampleCN: 它产生「仆人」与「服务」两词，不是这里的词根。

items.example: It adds the idea of watching over something.
items.exampleCN: 它加上「看住某物」的意思。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: The noun names both the act and its record.
items.exampleCN: 名词兼指行为与其记录。

items.example: The agent noun includes the mere onlooker.
items.exampleCN: 施事名词包括单纯旁观者。

items.example: The adjective also means careful in keeping rules.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词也指守规谨慎的。

items.meaning: the keeping of a rule or rite
items.example: It names practice, not perception.
The suffix names a place of work.

latinEntries.example: Latin servare means to keep or preserve.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 servare 意为保持、守护。

latinEntries.example: Latin ob- appears in obicere, to throw against.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 ob- 见于 obicere（扔向对面）。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 observare 意为看守、留意。

latinEntries.example: Latin observatio means a watching or a noting.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 observatio 意为观看、记录。

definition_zh: 观察者；观测人员；旁观者；列席观察员
definition_en: a person who watches or records something, especially for research, or an onlooker who takes no part in an event
core_image: 教室最后一排坐着一个人，只在本子上记录，从不举手，也不打断任何事
scene: 培训教室里，一位列席者坐在最后一排，只在本子上记录，从不打断讲课。The observer sat at the back and wrote down how often the teacher paused.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：只观看与记录、不参与其中的人；句意为这位观察者坐在后排，记下老师停顿的次数。图中可辨识物件：后排座位、记录本、秒表、讲台；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 观察者；观测员；旁观者；列席观察员（可数）

senses.title: A watcher who takes no part
senses.definition: a person who watches an event without joining in or changing it
senses.definitionCN: 观看事件、但不参与也不改变它的人
senses.example: The observer sat at the back and wrote down how often the teacher paused.
senses.exampleCN: 这位观察者坐在后排，记下老师停顿的次数。
senses.why: The word is built from the verb of watching plus the agent ending, so the person is defined by attention rather than action.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示观看的动词加施事词尾构成，因此这个人是被「注意」而非「行动」定义的。

senses.title: The recorder in a study
senses.definition: a researcher who watches and records behaviour or readings as part of a study
senses.definitionCN: 作为研究的一部分，观看并记录行为或读数的人
senses.example: A second observer checked the timings independently.
senses.exampleCN: 第二位观察者独立核对了计时。
senses.why: Two people watching the same session can compare notes, which is how a study shows that its records are reliable.
senses.whyCN: 两个人看同一场活动可以互相比对记录，研究正是以此证明记录可靠。

senses.title: The watcher in quantum theory
senses.definition: in quantum mechanics, the agent whose measurement fixes one of the possible outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 在量子力学中，其测量使某个可能结果确定下来的角色
senses.example: In quantum theory the observer cannot be left out of the account.
senses.exampleCN: 在量子理论里，观察者无法被排除在描述之外。
senses.why: If a measurement changes the state it measures, the watcher becomes part of the system, and the word carries that problem.
senses.whyCN: 如果测量改变了被测量的状态，观看者就成了系统的一部分，这个词正承担着这一难题。

senses.title: A seat without a vote
senses.definition: a representative allowed to attend and speak at a body but not to vote
senses.definitionCN: 获准出席并发言、但没有表决权的代表
senses.example: The body granted the agency observer status.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构给了这个组织观察员地位。
senses.why: An organisation that watches but does not decide needs a name between member and guest, and this is it.
senses.whyCN: 只看不决定的组织需要一个介于成员与客人之间的身份，这个词正好补上。

senses.title: The monitor at an election
senses.definition: a person sent to watch that a vote is conducted fairly and to report on it
senses.definitionCN: 被派去监督投票是否公正并提交报告的人
senses.example: An observer from each party stood at every ballot box.
senses.exampleCN: 每个投票箱旁都站着一名各党派的观察员。
senses.why: A watcher with a mandate to report turns looking into a safeguard, so the word gains a public function.
senses.whyCN: 负有报告职责的观看者把「看」变成一种保障，这个词于是有了公共职能。

senses.title: The researcher who joins in
senses.definition: in anthropology, a researcher who lives among the people studied while still recording
senses.definitionCN: 在人类学中与被研究者共同生活、同时坚持记录的研究者
senses.example: The observer joined the factory shift to understand the work.
senses.exampleCN: 这位观察者加入工厂班次，以理解那份工作。
senses.why: Some behaviour only appears to insiders, so the method accepts participation while trying to keep the record honest.
senses.whyCN: 有些行为只对内部人显现，因此这种方法允许参与，同时设法保持记录诚实。

senses.title: The impartial witness
senses.definition: a person present who can report what happened without a stake in the outcome
senses.definitionCN: 在场且与结果无利害关系、能陈述发生了什么的人
senses.example: To a neutral observer the mistake was obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 在中立的观察者看来，那个错误一目了然。
senses.why: Someone with no stake can be trusted to say what a participant cannot, and the word supplies that position.
senses.whyCN: 没有利害关系的人能说出参与者说不出口的话，这个词提供了这一位置。

senses.title: The officer at a ceasefire line
senses.definition: a soldier or official deployed to watch a truce or a disputed border and report violations
senses.definitionCN: 被派去监督停火或争议边界、并报告违规行为的军人或官员
senses.example: Military observers reported two breaches before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 军事观察员报告黎明前有两起违约。
senses.why: Where two sides will not share a patrol, a third party watches, and the watching is the whole job.
senses.whyCN: 双方不愿共同巡逻时，就由第三方来看，而「看」本身就是全部工作。

senses.title: A perceptive commentator
senses.definition: a person known for noticing and describing what others miss, often in public writing
senses.definitionCN: 以察觉并描述他人忽略之处著称的人，常见于公共写作
senses.example: She is a sharp observer of how committees really decide.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位敏锐的观察者，看得出委员会真正如何决定。
senses.why: Long practice in watching produces someone whose remarks are trusted, and the plain word for watcher becomes praise.
senses.whyCN: 长期观看的练习造就一个其评论可信的人，于是「观看者」这个朴素词成了赞誉。

intro.en: Observer is observe plus the agent ending -er, with Latin observator behind it. The science sense is early modern, and the quantum sense is a twentieth-century extension of it.
intro.cn: observer 是 observe 加施事词尾 -er 构成，背后有拉丁语 observator。科学观测义属近代早期，量子力学义则是二十世纪对它的延伸。

items.en: Observare meant to watch over and heed, from ob- 'over' and servare 'to keep'.
items.cn: observare 意为看守并留心，由 ob-「在……之上」与 servare「保持」构成。

items.en: Late Latin observator named the person who watched or kept a rule, a model for the English agent noun.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 observator 指观看或守规的人，为英语的施事名词提供了样板。

items.en: The English agent ending came from Old English -ere, itself borrowed from Latin -arius, so the two halves meet again.
items.cn: 英语施事词尾来自古英语 -ere，而 -ere 又借自拉丁语 -arius，两半在英语里重新汇合。

items.en: Observer entered English in the sixteenth century, at first for a person who keeps a rule or a custom.
items.cn: observer 在十六世纪进入英语，最初指遵守规则或习俗的人。

items.en: Seventeenth-century astronomy and natural history gave the word its recording sense, with instruments and notebooks.
items.cn: 十七世纪的天文学与博物学给了它「用仪器与记录本观看」的含义。

items.en: The twentieth century added the observer in quantum measurement and the observer sent to watch elections and ceasefires.
items.cn: 二十世纪又加上量子测量中的观察者，以及被派去监督选举与停火的观察员。

note.en: The first group shares the watching root; the second group names related onlooker roles.
note.cn: 第一组共享「观看」词根；第二组是相关的旁观角色。

entries.definition: The verb of watching, keeping and remarking.
entries.definitionCN: 表示观看、遵守与评论的动词。

entries.definition: The act or the recorded result of watching.
entries.definitionCN: 观看的行为，或被记录下来的结果。

entries.definition: Quick to notice; also careful about rules.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉敏锐的；也指守规谨慎的。

entries.definition: A building equipped for watching the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 装备起来观测天空的建筑。

entries.definition: The keeping of a rite or rule, not the person who watches.
entries.definitionCN: 对仪式或规则的遵行，不是观看的人。

entries.definition: Someone who watches an event without taking part; no scientific weight.
entries.definitionCN: 观看事件而不参与的人；没有科研分量。

entries.definition: A person who saw an event and can testify to it.
entries.definitionCN: 看见事件并能作证的人。

entries.definition: A person or device that keeps a continuous check.
entries.definitionCN: 持续进行检查的人或装置。

entries.definition: A member of an audience, there to be entertained.
entries.definitionCN: 观众之一，为观赏而来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin watcher, the real family and the fixed titles of research and missions.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语中的观看者、真实同族词，以及科研与派驻任务里的固定头衔。

normal.en: Observer is the verb of watching plus the person ending, and Latin already had a watcher noun.
normal.cn: observer 是观看动词加表示人的词尾，拉丁语里本就有「观看者」这一名词。

normal.en: The family runs observe, observation, observer, observant and observatory.
normal.cn: 同族词有 observe、observation、observer、observant 与 observatory。

normal.en: Research has a second observer check the timings, so the record can be trusted.
normal.cn: 研究中让第二位观察者核对计时，记录才可信。

normal.en: Elections and ceasefires both send observers, because a report needs a witness.
normal.cn: 选举与停火都派观察员，因为报告需要见证者。

normal.en: The observer effect names the trouble that watching can change what is watched.
normal.cn: 观察者效应命名「观看可能改变被观看之物」这一麻烦。

abstract.en: An observer is paid to be unnoticed, and noticed only in the report.
abstract.cn: 观察者的本分是不被注意，只在报告里被注意。

abstract.en: The best observer knows which detail would change the conclusion.
abstract.cn: 最好的观察者知道哪个细节会改变结论。

abstract.en: Watching without a stake is the quietest kind of power.
abstract.cn: 无利害关系的观看，是最安静的一种权力。

examples.en: Each observer recorded the same session on a separate sheet.
examples.cn: 每位观察者用各自的表格记录同一场活动。

examples.en: The observer noted that the queue moved faster after noon.
examples.cn: 观察者注意到中午之后队伍移动更快。

examples.en: An observer may speak at the meeting but may not vote.
examples.cn: 观察员可以在会上发言，但没有表决权。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「欧布泽弗」——守在旁边只看不插手的那个人：观察者

root: observe（拉丁语 observare「看守、留心」）+ 施事词尾 -er（古英语 -ere，借自拉丁语 -arius）；拉丁语本有 observator。科学义见于十七世纪，量子与政治观察员义为二十世纪延伸。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one silent watcher: the non-participant, the study recorder, the quantum measurer, the seat without a vote, the election monitor, the participant researcher, the impartial witness, the ceasefire officer and the perceptive commentator.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一个沉默的观看者：不参与者、研究记录者、量子测量者、无表决权席位、选举监督者、参与式研究者、公正见证者、停火军官与眼光锐利的评论者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure in the last row writes in a notebook and never raises a hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：最后一排的人在本子上记录，从不举手。

branches.en: THE ONLOOKER: present without a part, and trusted because there is no stake.
branches.cn: 旁观者：在场而不参与，因无利害而被信任。

branches.en: THE RESEARCH WATCHER: one of two recorders, or a researcher who lives among the studied.
branches.cn: 研究中的观看者：两名记录者之一，或与被研究者共同生活的研究者。

branches.en: THE MEASURER: the watcher whose act of watching enters the system being described.
branches.cn: 测量者：其观看动作进入了被描述系统的观看者。

branches.en: THE MANDATED WATCHER: a seat without a vote, a monitor at a ballot box, an officer on a truce line.
branches.cn: 受命观看者：无表决权的席位、投票箱旁的监督者、停火线上的军官。

branches.en: THE REMARKER: long watching turned into trusted comment.
branches.cn: 评论者：长期观看变成可信的评论。

intro.en: Observer is a Latin verb plus an agent ending that English borrowed twice over, once directly from Latin and once through Old English.
intro.cn: observer 是一个拉丁动词加施事词尾，而这个词尾被英语借了两次，一次直接来自拉丁语，一次经古英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is observare, servare and observator, with -or and -arius as agent endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 observare、servare 与 observator，施事词尾有 -or 与 -arius。

items.example: The person noun is built on the verb, not on a Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个表示人的名词建在动词上，而非拉丁名词上。

items.example: The verb supplies the action the person performs.
items.exampleCN: 动词提供这个人所做的动作。

items.example: It also gives preserve and reserve.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「保存」与「保留」两词的来源。

items.meaning: a watcher; a keeper of rules
items.example: Latin had the person noun before English did.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语先有这个人名词。

items.example: It builds observator, creator and narrator.
items.exampleCN: 它构成观察者、创造者与叙述者。

items.example: English prefers this ending for everyday agents.
items.exampleCN: 英语日常施事名词多用这个词尾。

items.example: It is the older shape behind the English ending.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语词尾背后更早的形态。

items.example: The noun names the activity, not the person.
The adjective describes the habit the person has.
items.exampleCN: 形容词描述这个人所具有的习惯。

items.example: The place noun extends the family to buildings.
items.exampleCN: 场所名词把词族扩展到建筑。

latinEntries.example: The verb is the direct source of observe.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个动词是 observe 的直接来源。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb servare (serv-, servatum; to keep)
latinEntries.example: It supplies the keeping and guarding idea.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它提供「看守、守护」这层意思。
拉丁语 observator 意为观看者。

latinEntries.example: Latin -or builds nouns such as doctor and rector.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -or 构成 doctor、rector 这类名词。

definition_zh: 障碍物；阻碍；障碍；绊脚石；壁垒
definition_en: something that stands in the way and must be removed, crossed or gone around before progress can continue
core_image: 一条小径正中横着一块大石，行人提着包从旁边的窄缝侧身挤过
scene: 山道正中倒着一棵大树，骑车的人只好下车，抬着车从路旁的草坡绕过去。A fallen tree became an obstacle on the mountain road.
sceneCN: 这里指挡在路上的实物（第 1 个义项：物理障碍物）；句意为倒下的树成了山道上的障碍。图中可辨识物件：横倒的树干、单车、草坡、被堵住的路面；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示路线的名词构成的复合说法，义为「障碍赛道」；本词没有常见的派生词族
由本词加表示比赛的名词构成的复合说法，义为「障碍赛」
本词的复数形式，义为「多处障碍」

senses.title: A physical thing blocking the way
senses.definition: an object that physically prevents passage along a route
senses.definitionCN: 物理上阻止人沿路线通行的物体
senses.example: A fallen tree became an obstacle on the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 倒下的树成了山道上的障碍。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to stand against; the noun first names a thing that literally stands in front of you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「站在对面」；这个名词最初指一件字面意义上立在你面前的东西。

senses.title: A hindrance to progress
senses.definition: a condition, rule or shortage that slows or prevents an intended outcome
senses.definitionCN: 减缓或阻止预期结果的条件、规则或短缺
senses.example: Lack of funding is the main obstacle to the research.
senses.exampleCN: 资金不足是这项研究的主要障碍。
senses.why: Once the thing standing in the way is no longer physical, the word keeps the same geometry: something is in front of the goal.
senses.whyCN: 当挡路之物不再有形，这个词仍保留同样的几何关系：有东西横在目标前面。

senses.title: A hurdle in sport
senses.titleCN: 体育比赛中的栏架与障碍
senses.definition: a fence, hurdle or water jump that a competitor must clear
senses.definitionCN: 选手必须越过的栏架、栅栏或水沟
senses.example: She cleared every obstacle in the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一圈越过了每一个障碍。
senses.why: Sport turns the blocking object into a designed test that must be jumped rather than removed.
senses.whyCN: 体育把挡路的物体变成设计好的考验：必须跳过，而不是搬走。

senses.title: A defensive barrier in warfare
senses.definition: a barricade, wire or ditch built to slow an advancing force
senses.definitionCN: 为迟滞对方推进而设置的路障、铁丝网或壕沟
senses.example: Engineers laid an obstacle belt before the position.
senses.exampleCN: 工兵在阵地前布设了一条障碍带。
senses.why: Here the obstacle is deliberately placed by the defender, so blocking becomes a tactic.
senses.whyCN: 这里的障碍由防守方故意设置，阻挡因此成为一种战术。

senses.title: A barrier to communication
senses.definition: a difference of language, culture or channel that keeps a message from arriving
senses.definitionCN: 语言、文化或渠道差异使信息无法抵达
senses.example: Poor translation created an obstacle between the two delegations.
senses.exampleCN: 糟糕的翻译在两个代表团之间造成了障碍。
senses.why: The thing in the way is now a gap in understanding rather than a stone.
senses.whyCN: 此时挡路的不再是石头，而是理解上的缺口。

senses.title: A mental barrier
senses.definition: an inner fear or belief that stops a person from acting
senses.definitionCN: 阻止人行动的内在恐惧或信念
senses.example: Fear of failure was the real obstacle, not the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 真正的障碍是对失败的恐惧，而不是考试。
senses.why: The stone moves inside the mind; the word follows it there.
senses.whyCN: 石头移进了心里；这个词也跟着去了那里。

senses.title: An economic or trade barrier
senses.definition: a tariff, quota or regulation that restricts the movement of goods
senses.definitionCN: 限制商品流动的关税、配额或法规
senses.example: The new tariff became an obstacle to exports.
senses.exampleCN: 新关税成了出口的障碍。
senses.why: Policy builds invisible walls, and the old stone word still fits them.
senses.whyCN: 政策筑起看不见的墙，这个古老的石头词依然适用。

senses.title: The sticking point in a negotiation
senses.definition: the one issue on which talks cannot move forward
senses.definitionCN: 使谈判无法推进的那一个议题
senses.example: Payment terms remained the chief obstacle to the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 付款条件仍是这笔交易的主要症结。
senses.why: In a room of words, one unresolved point can stand in the road like a boulder.
senses.whyCN: 在一屋子言辞里，一个未解决的议题也能像巨石一样横在路上。

senses.title: An object a machine must avoid
senses.titleCN: 机器必须避开的障碍物
senses.definition: an object detected by a vehicle or robot that must be routed around
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或机器人检测到、必须绕开的物体
senses.example: The robot stopped when its sensor detected an obstacle.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器检测到障碍物时，机器人停了下来。
senses.why: Robotics borrowed the plain physical sense and gave it a detection routine.
senses.whyCN: 机器人学借用了最朴素的物理义，并给它配上一套检测程序。

intro.en: Obstacle is a Latin verb for standing against, turned into a noun for the thing that stands in the way; English took it through French.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示「站在对面」的动词，转为指「挡在路上的东西」的名词；英语经法语借入。

items.en: stare meant to stand, to remain in place; it is the root of a large family of standing words.
items.cn: stare 意为「站立、留在原地」，是一大类「站立」词的词根。

items.en: ob- meant against, in front of, or towards, and it fixes the direction of the standing.
items.cn: ob- 意为「对着、在前面、朝向」，它规定了「站」的方向。

items.en: obstare was to stand in front of a person or thing, hence to hinder.
items.cn: obstare 意为「站在某人或某物前面」，因此引申为「阻碍」。

items.en: The noun obstaculum named the thing that stands in the way, not the act of standing.
items.cn: 名词 obstaculum 指挡在路上的那个东西，而不是「站」这个动作。

items.en: Old French obstacle carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century; the first date is approximate but the line is clear.
items.cn: 古法语 obstacle 在十四世纪把这个名词带进英语；首见年份为约数，但来源线索清楚。

items.en: Sport, trade, psychology and robotics each reused the stone-in-the-road image for a barrier of their own kind.
items.cn: 体育、贸易、心理学与机器人学各自把「路上的石头」这一意象用于本领域的壁垒。

note.en: The first group shares the standing root or looks close; the second group names nearby barriers and distinguishes how each one blocks.
note.cn: 第一组共享「站立」词根或形音相近；第二组是邻近的阻碍类词，说明中区分各自的阻挡方式。

entries.definition: Stubbornly refusing to change; it uses the same standing-against root for a person's will.
entries.definitionCN: 指固执地拒绝改变；用同一「站着对抗」词根来描述人的意志。

entries.definition: The medical field of childbirth; its Latin source named a midwife as one who stands before the mother.
entries.definitionCN: 指产科医学；其拉丁来源把助产士称为「站在母亲前面的人」。

entries.definition: To block or get in the way; it looks related but is built on a root meaning to pile up, not to stand.
entries.definitionCN: 指阻塞或挡路；形近，但其词根意为「堆起」，而非「站立」。

entries.definition: Several things standing in the way at once.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时挡在路上的多件东西。

entries.definition: A structure or rule that keeps things apart; it separates rather than merely blocking a route.
entries.definitionCN: 指把事物隔开的结构或规则；它重在分隔，而不只是挡住路线。

entries.definition: A small barrier to jump over, or a difficulty to pass; it suggests a sequence of tests.
entries.definitionCN: 指需跳过的矮栏，或需通过的难关；暗示一连串考验。

entries.definition: Something that slows progress, often a defect or burden carried along.
entries.definitionCN: 指拖慢进展的东西，常是随身带着的缺陷或负担。

entries.definition: An outside force crossing into a process and disturbing it; it acts on the process, not on the road.
entries.definitionCN: 指外部力量横插进一个过程并加以扰乱；它作用于过程，而非挡在路上。

entries.definition: A brake applied from inside a person or system; it restrains rather than stands in front.
entries.definitionCN: 指从人或系统内部施加的刹车；它重在拉住，而非立在前面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin stand-against image, the real sport and trade phrases, and the real sister roots.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「站着对抗」意象、真实的体育与贸易搭配，以及真实的同根词。

normal.en: ob- is against and stare is stand: an obstacle is something standing against your path.
normal.cn: ob- 是对着，stare 是站立：障碍就是立在路对面挡住你的东西。

normal.en: The word is a noun for the stone, not for the walking; remove the object and the road reopens.
normal.cn: 这个词是那块石头的名词，不是走路的名词；搬走物体，路就重新打开。

normal.en: Obstacle course and obstacle race are two real sporting phrases.
normal.cn: 障碍赛道与障碍赛是两个真实的体育说法。

normal.en: A trade tariff is an invisible obstacle, but the geometry is the same.
normal.cn: 贸易关税是一道看不见的障碍，但几何关系完全相同。

normal.en: A robot detects an obstacle and routes around it, which is the plain sense in a machine.
normal.cn: 机器人检测到障碍物并绕行，这就是这个词在机器里的朴素用法。

abstract.en: An obstacle is defined by the direction you want to go; the same stone is scenery to a walker heading elsewhere.
abstract.cn: 障碍是由你想去的方向定义的；同一块石头，对朝别处走的行人只是风景。

abstract.en: Some obstacles are placed on purpose, and some are only feared; both stop the feet.
abstract.cn: 有些障碍是故意设置的，有些只存在于恐惧中；两者都能让脚停住。

abstract.en: The word is not an enemy but a test of route: every path proves itself by what it goes around.
abstract.cn: 这个词不是敌人，而是对路线的检验：每条路都用它绕开的东西证明自己。

examples.en: The fallen bridge was the last obstacle between the village and the hospital.
examples.cn: 断桥是村庄与医院之间的最后一道障碍。

examples.en: High interest rates remain an obstacle to small businesses.
examples.cn: 高利率仍是小企业的障碍。

examples.en: The negotiators cleared the main obstacle with a single compromise.
examples.cn: 谈判者用一次妥协清除了主要症结。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥布斯脱克」——有东西「站在对面」挡着路

root: 来自拉丁语 obstaculum「阻碍物」← obstare「站在前面阻挡」← ob-「对着、在前」+ stare「站立」；经古法语 obstacle 于十四世纪进入英语。词源链清楚，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a stone in the road through abstract hindrance, sport, warfare, language, mind, trade and negotiation to a robot's detected object.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从路上的一块石头，经过抽象阻碍、体育、战争、语言、心智、贸易与谈判，最后落到机器人检测到的物体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boulder sits across a narrow path, and every walker must squeeze past its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块巨石横在窄路上，每个行人都要从它边缘挤过去。

branches.en: THE STONE AND THE WIRE: a physical object, whether natural or built for defence.
branches.cn: 石头与铁丝：自然存在的实物，或为防御而设的实物。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE TARIFF: an abstract condition or a policy wall in the way.
branches.cn: 规则与关税：抽象条件或政策之墙挡在路上。

branches.en: THE HURDLE AND THE SENSOR: an obstacle designed for sport or detected by a machine.
branches.cn: 栏架与传感器：为体育设计的障碍，或被机器检测到的障碍。

branches.en: THE WORD AND THE FEAR: a gap in understanding or a belief that stops the feet.
branches.cn: 话语与恐惧：理解上的缺口，或阻止脚步的信念。

branches.en: THE STICKING POINT: one unresolved issue that holds a whole deal in place.
branches.cn: 症结：一个未解决的议题把整笔交易卡住。

intro.en: Obstacle is a prepositional prefix plus a verb of standing plus a noun ending for a thing.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个方位前缀、一个「站立」动词，再加一个表「物」的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies stare, obstare and obstaculum; the English noun came through Old French with the same pieces.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 stare、obstare 与 obstaculum；英语名词经古法语而来，构件相同。

items.example: It fixes the direction of the standing.
The root names a body in place.
items.exampleCN: 词根命名一个立在原地的身体。

items.example: Prefix and root form the key verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成关键动词。

items.example: The noun names the thing, not the act.
It turns the verb into a concrete noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成具体名词。

items.example: The borrowed noun keeps the stone image.
items.exampleCN: 借入的名词保留石头意象。

items.example: The compound adds a designed route.
items.exampleCN: 复合词加上一条设计好的路线。

items.example: The compound adds competition.
A sister word applies the root to the will.
items.exampleCN: 同根词把这个词根用于意志。
